target_customer: Businesses and marketplaces that pay independent contractors, especially on-demand companies using Stripe Connect
problem: Companies managing contractors had manual onboarding, payments and 1099 tax filing. Payable automated these, and 1099 reporting became its most valued feature.
business_model: B2B SaaS priced per contractor per month, reported as 8 dollars in 2015

founders.name: Tad Milbourn
founders.background_notes: YC blog says the three founders met at Intuit.

founders.name: Peter Terrill
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in TechCrunch's 2017 Stripe acquisition article.

competitors.name: ZenPayroll
competitors.what: Payroll startup that added contractor payments in June 2013

technical_complexity.rationale: Time tracking, invoicing and 1099 generation are standard web and mobile engineering, with tax form rules as the main hard part.

defensibility.rationale: Tax filing data and the Stripe Connect integration created some stickiness, but Stripe could and did build the same feature in-house.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Stripe partnered with Payable in 2015 for 1099 forms for Connect users, then bought it on July 26, 2017 and said it would offer the features free in the Stripe Dashboard.

market_need_then: On-demand marketplaces such as Lyft and DoorDash had to file 1099s for many contractors. The Stripe partnership brought more users in early 2016 than the previous two years combined per Payable's co-founder.

branding.domain_note: payable.com now redirects to a Stripe support page about access ending.

rebrands.why: Shift from a free time tracking app to contractor payments and 1099s; the rename date was not found.

brand_strength.rationale: A descriptive name well matched to the payments product after the rename, but no brand coverage beyond fintech press.

pivots.from: Tiempo, a free time tracking app with fast employee pay
pivots.to: Payable, contractor onboarding, payments and 1099 compliance
pivots.why: Tax reporting and payments proved to be the valuable part; exact timing not sourced, but it had happened by August 2015.

outcome_analysis: Payable began as the time tracking app Tiempo in YC Summer 2014 and turned into a contractor payments and 1099 tool. It raised about 2.1 million dollars in 2015 and found distribution through a Stripe Connect partnership that fed on-demand marketplaces like Lyft and DoorDash. Stripe bought it on July 26, 2017 to bring 1099 reporting in-house, a classic platform acquisition of a niche feature vendor. The price was not disclosed.
notes: Round stage is not stated by the PYMNTS source so it is recorded as other. The 2.1 million figure matches CB Insights total of 2.12 million in a search snippet; General Catalyst is listed among backers on the YC page and in a General Catalyst post snippet. The August 2015 date is PYMNTS publication, and the round itself may have closed earlier. Competitors named by PYMNTS in 2015 were FreshBooks and QuickBooks (not dated at founding). ZenPayroll source is a TechCrunch headline from a search result, not opened. Founder education not found. Prior employer Intuit comes from the YC blog and PYMNTS only.
